answer: Require every agent identity to complete a periodic proof-of-work puzzle bound to a public registry. The work is cheap for one real agent but brutal at scale: forging ten thousand identities would cost an attacker more in electricity than any fraud could return. Legitimate agents' entries shine like ivory in the registry, while fakes leave a smudged, onyx-black trail of irregular timestamps - a pigment of suspicion that other agents can see and refuse to transact with.
